correctness.rationale: Orient each cube edge from its even-parity endpoint and generate it once from that endpoint and the changed bit, then sort by the frozen order key. Shared-endpoint edges cannot conflict in the triangle-free cube. For disjoint edges only the two cross-pairs of opposite parity can be joined; Hamming distance one exactly detects a connector in those pairs. The independent replay checked the literal 80-color list in RESULT.md against all 1120 conflicting pairs and obtained sorted class sizes 11,11,11,11,12,12,12. For the lower bound, edge transitivity lets any nonempty packing be moved to one through (0,1). A separate increasing-index enumeration, without the submitted coloring-based clique pruning, examined every anchor packing up through size 13 by intersecting the remaining compatibility lists and removing earlier indices. There were 51 compatible other edges, 12 packings of size 12 through the anchor and none of size 13. A still larger packing would include a 13-edge subpacking. Thus classes contain at most 12 edges, giving the lower bound ceil(80/12)=7. The checks use disjoint-connector conflicts, not proper or strong edge-color conflicts.
residual_risks: The replay is an exact finite proof for the specified cube and convention; it does not classify all partitions or cubes of other dimensions.

originality.rationale: Published catalogue results already prove the 12-edge packing bound and therefore the seven-color lower bound; neither is credited as new. The supported distinct finding is the injective edge index itself, proved by the global seven-class partition, with the more specific equitable sizes. The strongest inspected packing results concern the size and orbit of individual packs, not their partitioning into seven classes. The inspected general coloring bound does not come close to implying the upper bound. This is a best-of-knowledge assessment; it does not claim absolute priority.
residual_risks: The product-graph article remained inaccessible, and bounded searches do not exclude an unindexed equivalent partition or stronger cube theorem. The established prior packing bound is explicitly credited.

value.rationale: The five-cube is a natural symmetric product graph in the existing hypercube packing literature. Partitioning all 80 edges subject to the known two-step interference constraint is a different exact problem from finding one largest class, and a researcher working on injective edge coloring of cubes reasonably needs to know whether this packing-based lower bound is attainable in dimension five. The answer, with a balanced optimum witness, closes that specific gap rather than re-computing the known packing number. No broad product formula is claimed.
